condition.label: anterior cruciate ligament injury
condition.distinctions: ACL injury is not a single rehabilitation stage; graft choice, repair, stability and associated injury alter applicability.

scope.population: Clinically confirmed ACL injury; distinct acute management strategies and postreconstruction rehabilitation.
scope.stage: Acute/recent injury and staged postoperative rehabilitation must be identified; chronic symptomatic instability not fully covered.
scope.operativeStatus: Both nonoperative and reconstructed strategies researched; no interchangeable protocol.
scope.exclusions: Concomitant meniscus/collateral/cartilage injuries and surgical restrictions require separate assessment; professional/pediatric cohorts not covered by KANON.
scope.uncertainty: Research extraction only; no universal safe dose, clearance or diagnosis inferred.

sources.population: Active 18–35, ACLtear<=4 weeks, previously uninjured; professional athletes, low activity, complete collateral tear/full-thickness cartilage/extensive meniscal repair excluded.
sources.comparator: Rehab+early ACLR vs same rehab+optional delayed ACLR.
sources.coInterventions: Single-bundle patellar/hamstring reconstruction; meniscal procedures as indicated.
sources.outcomes: KOOS 4 improvement 42.9 early vs 44.9 optional; report presents difference 2.0 with CI−8.5, 4.5 (direction inconsistency retained), p.54. No strategy differenceOA/meniscal surgery; 51%optional group reconstructed.
sources.uncertainty: Managed strategies, not surgery-vs-no-rehab; crossovers; selected young active cohort; not unattended return-to-sport.
sources.harms: Four graft ruptures; two revisions; five contralateral reconstructions reported; not proof of equal individual injury risk.
sources.limitations: Managed strategies, not surgery-vs-no-rehab; crossovers; selected young active cohort; not unattended return-to-sport.

protocol.execution: Similar structured rehabilitation in both arms; exact exercise protocol referred to earlier report.
protocol.dose: not reported in this 5-year main article
protocol.frequency: not reported in this 5-year main article
protocol.supervision: Rehabilitation by physiotherapists; full visit schedule not given.
protocol.progression: Delayed ACLR for symptomatic ACL insufficiency with positive pivot shift; not time-alone clearance.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as exercise stop rule; instability required clinical management.

sources.design: Open-label multicenter strategy RCT, n 167, 163 completed.
sources.population: Adults 18–65, primary complete ACL rupture<=2 months; locked bucket-handle extension-deficit lesions excluded; associated injuries allowed.
sources.comparator: Early ACLR vs rehab with optional delayed surgery.
sources.outcomes: 24-monthIKDC 84.7vs 79.4, MD 5.3(95%CI 0.6, 9.9), statistically better early surgery, authors judge not clinically relevant. At 3 months rehab favored, MD−9.3(−14.6,−4.0); 50%rehab had ACLR.
sources.uncertainty: Unblinded, crossover, not equivalent to KANON population/outcome; cannot guarantee rehab-alone success or infer therapy harmful.
sources.harms: Early 4 reruptures+3 contralateral vs optional 2+1; small counts, exposure/treatment differences.
sources.limitations: Unblinded, crossover, not equivalent to KANON population/outcome; cannot guarantee rehab-alone success or infer therapy harmful.

protocol.execution: Supervised PT according to DutchACLguideline; exact exercise menu not reported.
protocol.dose: Minimum 3 months before considering elective delayed reconstruction.
protocol.supervision: Physical therapist supervised; postoperative PT until functional control.
protocol.progression: Clinical instability or failure to reach desired activity after>=3 months allowed ACLR.
protocol.stoppingRules: No numeric exercise stop rule; instability prompted clinical reassessment.

sources.design: Clinical practice guideline, systematic evidence+expert consensus; many recommendations low-certainty.
sources.population: After ACLR; isolated-surgery guidance must respect graft/surgical instructions and additional repairs.
sources.coInterventions: Multiple rehabilitation components; individual prescribing and monitoring.
sources.outcomes: Supports active rehabilitation; combines open/closed-chain strength and motor control. Running criteria are explicitly expert-proposed, not validated injury-risk thresholds; time alone insufficient.
sources.followUp: Heterogeneous source studies; no new follow-up.
sources.uncertainty: Postoperative evidence cannot be transferred directly to untreated ACL or multiligament/meniscal repair cases; no universal reps/load.
sources.harms: Monitor anterior knee pain/load; not conclusive running safety<=12 weeks.
sources.limitations: Postoperative evidence cannot be transferred directly to untreated ACL or multiligament/meniscal repair cases; no universal reps/load.

protocol.execution: Open-chain knee extension 90–45 degrees from week 4; legpress 0–45 degrees from week 3 for hamstring graft; static quads/SLR early options.
protocol.dose: not reported as one common sets/reps/load
protocol.frequency: not reported as one common frequency
protocol.supervision: Individual prescribed program and monitoring even when home-based.
protocol.progression: Criteria+minimum healing times+surgical restrictions; monitor pain/load response.
protocol.stoppingRules: Adjust anterior knee pain/loading; running criteria include full extension, 95%flexion, no/trace effusion, quadLSI>80%; expert-proposed, not app clearance.

findings.statement: Aspetar recommends individually prescribed and monitored rehabilitation, criteria-based progression with healing times; time alone is insufficient for return. No conclusive evidence running<=12 weeks is safe.

citations.location: Return to activities > Running; Box 5 recommendations

findings.applicability: Post ACLR, with surgical instructions and associated procedures considered.
findings.limitations: Expert criteria not validated automatic return thresholds; not an untreated ACLprotocol.

findings.statement: Aspetar permits limited-range open-chain knee extension 90–45 degrees from week 4 with anterior-knee-pain/load monitoring; early leg press 0–45 degrees from week 3 is hamstring-graft-specific.
findings.applicability: Post ACLR in described contexts, not all ACL injuries.
findings.limitations: Timing/range are clinical recommendations with low-certainty evidence; not independent fixed app limits.

exerciseMappings.matchRationale: Catalog leg-extension is generic weight_reps/Machine with repetition/load progression and does not encode postoperative stage, arc or surgical instructions. Separate clinical variation request prevents routine progression from substituting for rehabilitation.

proposedRules.statement: Candidate ordinary-workout gate: withhold automatic injured-knee progression and pivoting/jump return until the user has a clinician-defined injury/procedure stage and permitted activities; never infer clearance from weeks elapsed or historicalACLselection alone.

citations.location: Return to activities > Running; Box 5 recommendations

applicability.population: Clinically confirmed ACL injury; distinct acute management strategies and postreconstruction rehabilitation.
applicability.stage: Especially acute injury or incomplete postoperative rehabilitation.
applicability.rationale: Guideline requires individual prescribing/monitoring and functional progression; this product gate handles unknown clinical stage.

proposedRules.limitations: Product precaution, not a published lifetime exercise ban; scope includes nonoperative injury indirectly, so review required. No supported-condition release.

proposedRules.statement: Retain restricted-arc knee extension as a post ACLR clinical-review candidate only after graft, associated surgery and stage are verified. Do not use the source timing as automatic clearance.

applicability.population: Clinician-managed post ACLR patients matching the guideline.
applicability.stage: Postoperative stage and surgical instructions known.
applicability.rationale: Source supplies a stage-specific option, not generic evidence all leg extension is safe or harmful.

proposedRules.limitations: Exact load/dose/resistance setup unresolved; competing joint limits and other diagnoses still govern.

gaps: Researcher appraisal, not formal GRADE: moderate confidence in managed strategy comparisons; low confidence in unsupervised exercise dosage or automated return criteria. Product gates require independent review.
KANON andCOMPAREcompare managed strategies with optional surgery, not free exercise versus surgery.
Early running/pivoting safety and return-to-sport thresholds not established for an unsupervised app; Aspetar criteria explicitly proposed, not fully validated.
Detailed KANON/COMPAREexercise menu/dose is in referenced protocols not retrieved; no schedule invented.
Aspetar postoperative ROM/timing options cannot be applied to untreated ACL or additional repair without clinical instructions.
Independent clinical review absent; doses are reported study protocols, not app prescriptions.
No universal contraindication follows from trial exclusion or another exercise showing benefit. No generic five-second progression or stretch strength-set credit.
